companyDescription: Custom AI Silicon leader · 6 hyperscaler XPU programs · $73B AI backlog · Tomahawk 6 networking · VMware Cloud Foundation
priceNote: Down 20% from Jun 3 ATH $495 — post-earnings selloff creates 34% upside window to analyst consensus $524
summary: Broadcom fell 20% from its June 3 ATH of $495 despite beating Q2 FY2026 (EPS $2.17, AI revenue +143% YoY) because Q3 AI chip guidance of $16B was below the whisper number. The pullback restores 34% upside to analyst consensus $524, with $73B in AI backlog across 6 hyperscalers (OpenAI confirmed as 6th) and Q3 FY2026 earnings on Sep 3 as the next catalyst.

catalysts.name: OpenAI 'Jalapeño' — 6th Hyperscaler XPU
catalysts.description: CEO Hock Tan confirmed OpenAI as 6th major XPU customer with a $10B+ custom inference ASIC entering mass production late 2026. Expands $73B AI backlog to a new customer tier.

catalysts.name: Q3 FY2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Company guided $29.4B total revenue (+84% YoY) / $16B AI chips (+200%+ YoY). Beat bar = AI chips >$17B or 7th hyperscaler announced. Options imply ±7.45% move.

catalysts.name: Tomahawk 6 / Jericho 4 — Volume Production
catalysts.description: Industry-first 102.4 Tbps Tomahawk 6 Ethernet switch in volume production. Jericho 4 connecting 1M+ XPU clusters. AI networking pricing power catalyst.

catalysts.name: FY2027 $100B Revenue Target
catalysts.description: Hock Tan targeting $100B+ FY2027 — would make Broadcom the first semiconductor company to reach that milestone. Each earnings is a checkpoint.

risks: Whisper number risk — Q3 guide is $16B AI chips; buy-side likely modeling $17–18B; miss-vs-whisper repeats Jun 3 -12.59% pattern
Valuation at 62x TTM PE — guidance must consistently raise the ceiling, not just meet it
Customer concentration — 6 hyperscalers = essentially all AI semiconductor revenue; one capex slowdown = direct hit
In-house chip competition — Google TPU, Amazon Trainium, Apple MTIA could reduce AVGO's TAM over time
Rate sensitivity — $1.8T market cap at 62x PE; highly sensitive to Fed hawkish surprise or long-end rate spike
US export controls — ByteDance/China exposure creates ongoing regulatory risk
Power grid bottleneck — US data center power constraints delay hyperscaler capex → delay AVGO orders

estimateDates.note: Revenue guide $29.4B total / $16B AI chips — true beat bar is AI >$17B or 7th hyperscaler announcement
$10B+ custom inference ASIC entering production — first direct OpenAI silicon revenue recognition

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed at 3.50–3.75%; rate-sensitive at 62x TTM PE. Any hike signal at Jul 29 FOMC compresses multiples rapidly — Jun 3 -12.59% on a nominal beat shows the template.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE 3.4% (3-yr high). Hyperscaler capex is driven by competitive AI positioning, not cyclical demand — partially insulated from inflation.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: AI networking and custom silicon demand is structural. The near-term risk is investor expectations management, not fundamental demand slowdown.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — 62x PE and investor skittishness on guidance is the primary risk. Fundamental AI demand (6 hyperscaler XPU programs + $73B backlog) remains intact.
